findings.severity: local logical wording, not a failure of the main theorem
findings.title: Ergodicity is sufficient, not necessary, for constant Lyapunov data
findings.observed_text: 不要求 #{\mu} 遍历；遍历时各指数及其重数才几乎处处为常数。
findings.issue: The word '才' presents ergodicity as necessary for almost-everywhere constant exponents and multiplicities. Oseledets gives invariant data; ergodicity ensures constancy, but the converse fails.
findings.counterexample: Let f be the identity on a positive-dimensional compact manifold and let mu=(delta_p+delta_q)/2 with p!=q. The set {p} is invariant with measure 1/2, so mu is not ergodic. Nevertheless Df^n is the identity, and all Lyapunov exponents equal zero everywhere with multiplicity dim(M).
findings.corrected_math: 不要求测度遍历。若测度遍历，则各 Lyapunov 指数及其重数几乎处处为常数；非遍历时也可能恰为常数。
findings.source: OSELEDETS-AUTHOR-EXPOSITION, invertible case, Theorem 4; the necessity counterexample is calculated directly.
findings.suggested_edit: Replace the necessity-implying '才' by an explicit sufficient-condition statement. No displayed formula needs changing.
findings.verified_replacement: 不要求 #{\mu} 遍历；若测度遍历，则各指数及其重数几乎处处为常数。

verified_checks.checked: Independent s-parameter unfolding; dissipativity; degree at most s-1; error controlled for r<1/epsilon; symplectic b=1 alternative.
Counts hyperbolic fixed points of f^k, not exact-period orbits. Arbitrary prescribed thresholds are exceeded infinitely often. Finite-regularity attribution is separated from the smooth argument.
Finite 1<=r<infinity; annulus local diffeomorphisms or global dimension >=3; generic families, every parameter, infinitely many periods. No common parameter-independent subsequence asserted.
Simple elliptic spectrum, stated low-order nonresonances and invertible Birkhoff twist matrix retained; nondegenerate elliptic locus is open.
Compact parameter manifold, jointly smooth families inside the nondegenerate open locus; dense/open-dense/residual distinctions and every-parameter quantifier retained.
Smooth universality uses the same open locus and all-parameter quantifier; countable-base argument cites openly localizable targets.
verified_checks.source: BT25b-v1 Theorem C, Theorem E, Proposition 1.5

verified_checks.checked: Smooth surface theorem; elliptic point implies approximation by positive-entropy maps. The derivative-norm entropy formula is restricted to surfaces. Analytic extensions remain open questions, not proved consequences of universality.
verified_checks.source: SIAM Section 2.3, Theorem 2.15 and subsequent problems

verified_checks.checked: Compact C^1 invertibility supplies both integrability assumptions. Norm equivalence gives the stated 2 log(C)/n bound. The invariant full-measure splitting needs no ergodicity. Operator-norm growth is the maximal exponent. Area preservation forces the two exponents to sum to zero, hence the maximum is nonnegative.
verified_checks.source: OSELEDETS-AUTHOR-EXPOSITION, Theorem 4; elementary norm comparison and determinant calculation checked independently.

source_caveats.classification: source inconsistency, not an inspected writer error
source_caveats.observation: Theorem A calls growth super exponential but prints limsup log(#Per_k(f))/log(k)=+infinity.
source_caveats.mathematical_correction: That formula alone is weaker than superexponential growth: exponential counts satisfy it. The usual subsequential superexponential condition is limsup log(#Per_k(f))/k=+infinity.
source_caveats.editorial_action: When discussing this theorem, distinguish the printed formula from the stronger growth assertion; justify any stronger reformulation instead of silently changing the quotation. Actual 311C concerns Lyapunov exponents and does not make this growth claim.
